prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a top-down view of a salon interior where a seated person's foil-covered head is directly below and in front of the standing camera wearer at about 0.4–0.6 metres (brightest foreground), flanked on the right within arm's reach (0.6–0.9 metres) by a tray table holding a dye bowl, foil, and a towel, and an empty salon chair at 1.0–1.3 metres. Beyond the seated client at roughly 1.5–2.5 metres are wall mirrors, drawer cabinets, and in frame 3 a second worker crouching on the left about 1.2–1.5 metres away near the client's extended foot and blue foot-bath basin, with the client and workers facing away from or downward relative to the camera wearer rather than looking up. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's black-gloved left arm enters the foreground in frames 4 and 5 at 0.2–0.4 metres (pure white), partially occluding the client's head and sitting roughly 0.4 metres to the left of the right-hand dye bowl. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground head, mid-ground tray and chair armrests, and receding wall cabinets into distinct distance layers despite complex visual clutter. However, the map is unreliable on the wall mirrors, where virtual reflections of the salon chair, foot basin, and opposite room are rendered with false recessed depth (2.5–3.5 metres) instead of the flat planar surface of the mirror glass at ~1.6 metres.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to capture most of the salon layout, detecting objects only in frames 1, 3, and 4 while leaving frames 2 and 5, as well as all background mirrors, cabinets, trays, and chairs, completely unsegmented. In frame 1, it detects the seated client's head in the lower-left foreground (~0.5 metres from the camera wearer, within arm's reach) but misclassifies the foil-wrapped hair as a 'couch' while labeling only a tiny sliver of the client's lower-left leg/foot at ~1.2 metres as 'person'. In frame 3, as the camera turns slightly left, the second worker crouching at ~1.3 metres on the upper-left facing the client's outstretched foot (within that worker's arm's reach, ~0.8 metres from the client's torso) is misclassified as a 'dog', while the client and foreground tools are missed entirely. In frame 4, the map correctly segments the combined silhouette of the camera wearer's reaching left arm (0.2–0.4 metres) and the client's occluded head (0.5 metres) as a single 'person' mask, though it merges the two individuals together and misses the camera wearer's right hand by the dye bowl. While the mask boundary in frame 4 sharply isolates the foreground human silhouette from the dark floor and chair background, the segmentation map is highly unreliable due to severe top-down perspective distortion, heavy occlusion by hair foils and capes, and false or merged class labels.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost entirely blank across the five-frame sequence, detecting a single yellow body skeleton only in the upper-left quadrant of frame 3 and nothing in frames 1, 2, 4, or 5. In frame 3, this skeleton localizes the second person crouching on the floor about 1.2–1.5 metres to the left-front of the camera wearer and roughly 0.8 metres in front of the seated client, oriented toward the lower-right where the client's lower legs extend into a foot basin within that person's arm's reach. The plotted head, torso, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, and knee keypoints show this crouching person angled downward toward the client's foot and facing away from the camera wearer. Compared to the dark clothing and awkward top-down angle in the RGB strip, the skeleton in frame 3 clarifies the compact, bent-knee posture and arm reach of the crouching worker. However, the pose map is largely unreliable for this steeply angled egocentric scene, completely missing the seated client directly below the camera (0.4–0.6 metres, occluded by hair foils and a cape), failing to track the crouching worker when partially cut off by the frame edge in other frames, and detecting no magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's black-gloved hands reaching at 0.2–0.6 metres in frames 1 through 5.
